name: KUMITATE Site Tools
author: MOTOKI

sections.description:
KUMITATE Site Tools adds site building features to any block theme, one switch at a time. Nothing is enabled for you: open Settings and turn on only what a site needs.

The plugin extends core blocks instead of replacing them. Table settings are stored in the standard className, and the bundled patterns are built from core blocks only, so a page keeps working as ordinary block content after the feature is switched off or the plugin is deactivated.

Features, grouped by tab:

  • Table reading aids. Horizontal scrolling, a header row kept in view, a minimum width for every column, first-column emphasis and cell merging for the core table block, set from the block sidebar with no class names to type. Merged cells and header cells are saved as standard table markup (colspan, rowspan, th), so they stay when the plugin is off.
  • Pricing, services and contact patterns. Generic layouts for any trade, built from core blocks. Replace the text, photos and links on the page.
  • Image slide block. Add, replace and reorder core image blocks inside a slide. Autoplay is off by default, pauses on hover, focus and hidden tabs, and does not run when the visitor asks for reduced motion.
  • Breadcrumbs block. A real page and category hierarchy, never an invented primary category. Place it in the Site Editor, or let the KUMITATE theme position it for you.
  • Post sharing block for LINE, X and Facebook, shown on single posts, with an optional Copy URL button that confirms the copy on screen and to screen readers and falls back to a selected text box where copying is not available.
  • Table of contents block. Lists the page’s headings (H2, H2-H3 or H2-H4) with anchors added when the page is shown, numbered or plain, hidden below a chosen number of headings.
  • Link card block. Pick a post, page, category or tag by title; the card shows its image, title and summary, which can be replaced with your own, as a card, a slim line or plain text. It outputs nothing for a draft, private, removed or password-protected post.
  • Related pages list block. Posts from the same category or tag, or the child or sibling pages of a page, as cards, a list with small images or plain links, with the number, order, columns for phones and computers, a heading, the summary and the date. Built when the page is shown, in the content or in a Site Editor template; only published posts without a password are listed.
  • Automatic table of contents: added before the first heading of posts or other chosen types, when the page is shown. Left out where a table of contents block is placed or the page turns it off.
  • Automatic link cards: an address of a post or page of this site, pasted on its own line or embedded, is shown as a link card. Addresses of other sites are left alone and never fetched.
  • Structured data as one connected graph: publisher, WebSite, WebPage, BreadcrumbList and BlogPosting joined by @id. It works alongside SEO SIMPLE PACK and turns itself off when another plugin outputs structured data, so pages never carry two copies.
  • Analytics and site verification: fields for a Google Analytics 4 measurement ID, a Google Tag Manager container ID and the Search Console and Bing verification codes. Only the IDs are entered and checked; the plugin writes the tags. Nothing is output on admin screens, the login screen, feeds or the REST API.
  • Remove unneeded output: stop the emoji script, the WordPress version, the RSD, shortlink, REST API, embed discovery and feed links, and pingbacks to your own posts, one item at a time. Nothing is ticked by default.
  • Excerpt for pages: the excerpt box on pages, used in link cards, lists and the meta description.
  • Post list columns: featured image and search visibility columns in the post and page lists, with quick and bulk editing of search visibility. The search column is left out while another SEO plugin is in charge.
  • Search and sharing for sites without an SEO plugin: search titles and meta descriptions, Open Graph and X card tags, and noindex with the WordPress sitemap following it. Off by default, and they step aside for the major SEO plugins.
  • Accordion block. Items built on the browser’s own details and summary elements, so they open with a click, Enter or Space and can be read without JavaScript; the script only adds an animation and stays still when the visitor asks for reduced motion. Four styles, three CSS-drawn icon sets, titles as plain text or h2 to h6, and items that start open.
  • FAQ block. Questions and answers marked Q and A, in four styles, with square, rounded or round marks in the text color, the main color or a custom color, outlined or filled. Optional FAQPage structured data: one script per page built from the blocks.
  • Description list block. Terms and descriptions saved as dl, dt and dd, stacked, with a line on the left, side by side (term width 1 to 12em, stacked on phones) or as banded terms.
  • Tab block. Three styles, tab widths and sideways scrolling set separately for computers and phones, a first-open tab, background color and four border sets. Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with arrow, Home and End keys; without JavaScript every panel is shown in turn with its title.
  • Step block. Numbered steps saved as an ordered list, in three styles, with the first number, number shape or layout, a translatable label and the title element set on the list, and per-step overrides. A timeline style joins dates or times with a line, for a history, the flow of a day or an event programme, with an icon, fill, emphasis or color for each point.
  • Caption box block. A framed box with a caption, in seven styles and three color sets a theme can redefine with CSS custom properties. Kinds (information, hint, caution, alert, good example, bad example, memo) set the icon, color and caption at once, with colors made from the theme; an icon can also be added without a kind.
  • Speech balloon block. A face image, a name and the words in a balloon, speaking or thinking, filled or outlined. Saved speakers copy their image, name and look into a balloon, so editing a speaker never changes published posts.
  • Review block. A rating in half stars, points for and against, a summary, a price and a link, with optional Review structured data for products, services, shops, apps, books and courses.
  • Banner link block. A card with a title and a short text over a background image, all one link, with the text position, an overlay, a shape for computers and phones and a hover effect that respects reduced motion.
  • Box menu block. Linked boxes in a grid, each with an icon or an image and a label, with separate column counts for phones and computers.
  • Link list block. Links with an icon, lines between them and an optional arrow at the end.
  • Icon block. One large icon from the shared set, with a size, a color from the theme palette, a background shape (none, circle or rounded square; light, filled or outline), alignment, an optional link and a name for screen readers. Only the icon name is saved.
  • Icons: 34 line icons drawn for this plugin, no brand logos. Posts save only the icon’s name, so icons can be added or replaced with the siteframe_site_tools_icons filter.
  • Responsive columns block. One to six columns each for phones, tablets and computers, or a sideways scroll on phones that works with the keyboard. Converts to and from the core columns block.
  • Full-width section block. A background that reaches the screen edges on full-width templates, with an optional image, a tint and slanted, waved, peaked, arched or zigzag top and bottom edges. A separate background image and focal point can be set for phones; visitors download only one of the two.
  • Display conditions block. Shows the blocks inside only to logged-in or logged-out visitors, to chosen roles, within a period, on chosen kinds of page or for chosen categories and tags. Not a way to protect paid content. Placed blocks keep their conditions when the feature is off.
  • Show on phones or computers only: a block setting saved as an additional CSS class. The hiding styles keep loading on pages that use it even when the feature is switched off, so content never appears twice. The breakpoint follows the theme (782px) and can be filtered.
  • Space below blocks: a toolbar menu that sets a block’s bottom margin from the theme’s spacing sizes, stored as the core margin setting, and a panel with the space above and below for computers, tablets and phones. The computer size is core’s own margin, so it stays without the plugin.
  • Text highlights: marker, font size, small note, no line break, folder and file names, list lines and centred lines in table cells, a line break on phones only, letter spacing (narrow, wide or very wide) and a button that clears formatting. The formats stay registered when the feature is off, so saved text keeps its markup.
  • Format sets and editor settings: a KUMITATE > Editor settings screen for the marker shape and colors, three named format sets that apply several formats in one click, and up to ten custom formats whose classes you style in Additional CSS.
  • Block style collection: boxes, icon boxes, frames, border sets, list marks, section headings, image and video frames, a double-line table and framed columns for core blocks, colored by the theme. Only a class is saved, so styled blocks keep their content when the feature is off, and the CSS loads only on pages that use a style.
  • Your own block styles: name a style, choose the blocks it is offered on and pick its colors, border, corner radius, spacing, shadow and text size from a form, with a live preview. It appears under Styles in those blocks and is saved as the standard is-style-{name} class. Up to 20 styles.
  • Button styles and inline buttons: Raised, Rounded, Shadow, With arrow and Shine styles, an icon, a hover effect (lift, lighter, darker, moving arrow) that respects reduced motion and a width for phones, tablets and computers for the core button block, and linked text shown as a small button inside a line.
  • Column options for phones: two columns on phones and the space between stacked columns for the core columns block, saved as classes.
  • Editor helpers: a title length counter, a button that selects the parent list, and a per-user choice of which KUMITATE text toolbar buttons appear.
  • Per-page display settings (off by default): a “Display” panel in the post and page editor hides the title, featured image, date, categories, tags and author, sharing links, breadcrumbs or the fixed contact bar on that page only. Lists of posts and query loops are not affected. A hidden title stays available to screen readers and search engines unless the text has its own level 1 heading.
  • Default featured image: an image shown for posts without a featured image in query loop lists, link cards and related pages lists. Nothing is saved to the posts, and it is never used for sharing images or structured data.
  • Fixed contact bar block. Booking, telephone and LINE buttons kept at the bottom of the screen, on phones only or on every screen size, without JavaScript. Place it in the footer to show it on every page.
  • Business info block. Name, address, telephone, opening hours, a map link and a reservation button, described to search engines as a local business of the chosen type with the same details.
  • Settings export and import on the Get started tab: one JSON file with the plugin’s settings. Import checks every value like the settings screens and ignores unknown keys.

Colors, fonts and spacing come from the active theme’s presets. The plugin does not restyle body text or headings, and its CSS is scoped to its own blocks.

No license key, no domain activation, no purchase check, no expiry. Deactivating the plugin never deletes content or settings. No external fonts and no tracking by the plugin itself. Nothing is loaded from other servers unless you enter a Google Analytics or Google Tag Manager ID (see External services).

The plugin is optional for the KUMITATE theme and works with other block themes. Breadcrumbs and sharing are placed automatically in the KUMITATE theme’s templates; other themes can use the siteframe_breadcrumbs and siteframe_share shortcodes.

External services

This plugin connects to outside services only when you switch on Analytics and site verification and enter an ID. Nothing is sent while the feature is off or the fields are empty.

  • Google Analytics 4: with a measurement ID, every public page loads the Google tag (gtag.js) from www.googletagmanager.com, which sends visit data such as the page address, referrer, browser and device information to Google Analytics. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Google Tag Manager: with a container ID, every public page loads the container from www.googletagmanager.com, which runs the tags you set up in Tag Manager and sends the data those tags collect. Terms, Privacy Policy.

The Search Console and Bing verification codes are only written into a meta tag in the page head; the plugin sends nothing to Google or Microsoft for them.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open KUMITATE in the admin menu and enable the features you want. Each tab saves on its own and leaves the other tabs alone.
sections.faq:
What happens to my content when I turn a feature off?

Saved content and settings stay. A switched-off feature stops offering new insertions and stops applying its own styles, and existing blocks remain editable. Table settings can still be removed after the feature is off.

What happens when I deactivate the plugin?

Core blocks and patterns keep working, because they were saved as standard block content. The image slide block needs the plugin to be active again before it can be edited. Nothing is deleted.

Do I need the KUMITATE theme?

No. The plugin works with block themes in general. The KUMITATE theme places breadcrumbs and sharing in its templates automatically; elsewhere use the shortcodes.

Does it require an account, key or subscription?

No. There is no activation, no purchase check and no call home.

Does it add structured data on top of my SEO plugin?

No. The structured data feature disables itself when a major SEO plugin is active. Turn it off by hand if another source outputs the same markup.

Does it add meta tags on top of my SEO plugin?

No. Search titles, descriptions, sharing tags and noindex output nothing while Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework or SEO SIMPLE PACK is active. A theme or other plugin printing the same tags cannot always be detected, so check a page’s source after switching.

What happens to the new blocks when their feature is switched off?

They leave the block inserter, and every placed block keeps showing and stays editable. Blocks set to show on phones or computers only stay hidden where chosen, so nothing appears twice.

Can I merge table cells?

Yes. Select a table and open “Merge and convert cells” in the block sidebar. Merged cells are saved as standard colspan and rowspan attributes, so they stay if the plugin is switched off or removed.

Does changing a format set change text I already formatted?

No. A format set is a shortcut: it applies bold, italic, the core highlight color, the marker and the size as separate formats, and nothing in the saved text refers to the set. The marker shape and colors are different: they are CSS variables, so changing them updates every marker on the site.

I hid the title of a page. Is the page left without a heading?

No. When the text of the page has no level 1 heading, the title is kept in the page for screen readers and search engines and only hidden from sight. When the text has its own level 1 heading, the title is removed so the page has one main heading. The browser tab title, search results title and structured data are not changed.

Does hiding a part of a page change my content?

No. The choice is stored as post meta and the part is left out when the page is shown. Switching the feature off shows everything again; saved choices are kept.

Can the display conditions block protect members-only or paid content?

No. It only chooses what is shown. The blocks inside are saved in the post, so anyone who can edit the post can read them, site search finds the post by their words, and removing the plugin shows them to everyone. Pages with the block ask caches not to store them; check that your caching plugin respects this. Switching the feature off keeps the conditions of placed blocks.

Can I use my own icons?

Yes. The siteframe_site_tools_icons filter adds or replaces icons by name. Posts store only the name, so a replaced icon changes everywhere it is used without invalid blocks. Icon markup is limited to basic shapes; anything else is removed.

Will the review block show stars in Google?

It writes Review structured data when both the block’s switch and KUMITATE structured data are on. Google decides whether to show stars, and never shows them for a review a business writes about itself on its own site. When an SEO plugin writes the page’s structured data, each review is written as a separate item.

Where do I put my own CSS or code?

The plugin does not save CSS, JavaScript or HTML typed by hand. Put CSS in WordPress’s Additional CSS (Appearance > Editor > Styles > Additional CSS, or the Customizer in a classic theme). Analytics and verification tags have their own ID fields. For other code, use your theme’s functions.php or a plugin made for adding code. CSS and code saved by version 0.16 or earlier are kept but no longer output; the admin shows them once so you can move them.

What happens to blocks using my own style if I rename or delete it, or switch the feature off?

Renamed: blocks using an earlier class name keep the look. Switched off: the style is no longer offered, but blocks already using it keep their look. Deleted: the blocks keep the class but lose the look.

Do my existing steps and caption boxes change?

No. The timeline and the caption box kinds are new options whose defaults save the same markup as before, so placed blocks stay valid and look the same.

Where do the page, category and tag conditions apply?

To the page being viewed, so a display conditions block in a header or footer template part follows each page. REST responses and feeds have no page being viewed, so content with these conditions is left out there.

Does the default featured image change my posts or sharing images?

No. It is shown only in lists of posts, link cards and related pages lists. Nothing is saved to the posts, and sharing images and structured data keep using each post’s own image and the default sharing image.

What does a settings export contain?

The features switched on and off, search and sharing settings, site identity, the automatic table of contents, editor settings, removed output, the default featured image, the sharing options, the analytics and verification IDs and your own block styles. Posts, pages, images and per-page settings are not included. Image choices are not carried over from another site’s file, because images have different IDs there.
sections.changelog:
0.18.0

  • Get started: a strip at the top shows the three parts of KUMITATE (the free theme, this plugin, a trade child theme) with what is done and the one thing to do next.
  • After a child theme is activated, the pointer to its finished sample shows on every admin screen for a week, until the sample is created or dismissed. Earlier “Not now” answers are forgotten when the theme changes.
  • No change to features, blocks or saved settings.

0.17.0

  • Settings no longer accept free-form CSS, JavaScript or HTML. Custom CSS, CSS per page and CSS for custom formats are retired: saved CSS is no longer output and is shown once in the admin so you can move it to Additional CSS.
  • Code in the page head and body becomes fields for a Google Analytics 4 measurement ID, a Google Tag Manager container ID and site verification codes. Saved code is no longer output and is shown once in the admin.
  • Your own block styles are built from a form (colors, border, radius, spacing, shadow, text size and weight) instead of CSS.
  • Works with the hooks of the KUMITATE theme 0.12.14 and later for per-page display settings and breadcrumbs.
  • Translations are no longer bundled; they come from translate.wordpress.org.
  • Settings are checked field by field when saved.

0.16.0

  • New blocks: icon, and a related pages list of posts from the same category or tag, child pages or sibling pages.
  • New under Design: your own block styles and a default featured image for posts without one.
  • New on the SEO tab: code in the page head and body (users allowed unfiltered HTML only), removal of unneeded output item by item, and the excerpt for pages.
  • New on the Get started tab: settings export and import as one JSON file.
  • Step block: a timeline style with a date or time per item. Caption box: kinds with an icon, color and caption, and an optional icon beside the caption.
  • Display conditions: kinds of page, categories and tags.
  • Space below blocks: space above and below for computers, tablets and phones.
  • Full-width section: a background image for phones.
  • Core button: hover effects and a width for each screen size.
  • Text highlights: letter spacing. Custom formats go up to ten; the two saved ones are unchanged.
  • Post sharing: an optional Copy URL button.
  • Light bulb, pencil and exclamation mark icons in the shared set.
  • The recommended settings on the Get started tab also switch on the icon block, the related pages list, the default featured image and the excerpt for pages.
  • All new features and options are off until switched on. Existing blocks save the same markup, and nothing new is loaded from other servers.

0.15.0

  • New blocks under Blocks: speech balloon with saved speakers, review with optional Review structured data, banner link, box menu, link list, responsive columns, full-width section and display conditions.
  • New under Design: block style collection, button styles and inline buttons, column options for phones, per-page CSS and editor helpers.
  • New under Navigation: automatic table of contents and automatic link cards for addresses of this site.
  • New on the SEO tab: post list columns for the featured image and search visibility, with quick and bulk editing.
  • Link card: categories, tags and other terms, your own title, summary and image, and slim and text-only styles. Existing cards look as before.
  • Text highlights: folder and file names, list lines and centred lines in table cells, and a line break on phones only.
  • Rich text toolbar: a KUMITATE group with a Decoration menu (clear formatting, folder and file names, small note, text and background color, inline button, no-wrap, line break on phones, custom formats and format sets), inline icons, font size and marker. Each user chooses which buttons sit on the toolbar and which in the menu.
  • Text and background color use the core highlight format, so colors stay when the plugin is off.
  • All blocks of the plugin are grouped under a KUMITATE category at the top of the inserter, with short titles.
  • Shared line icons with a searchable picker, replaceable with the siteframe_site_tools_icons filter.
  • The recommended settings on the Get started tab include the new features, except the review block, display conditions, per-page CSS and the automatic table of contents.
  • All new features are off until switched on. Nothing new is loaded from other servers.

0.14.0

  • New: Format sets and editor settings (off by default). KUMITATE > Editor settings sets the marker shape and four colors, three named format sets and two custom formats with CSS for the front end and the editor. Custom formats stay registered and their CSS keeps loading when the feature is off.
  • New: Per-page display settings (off by default). Hide the title, featured image, post details, sharing links, breadcrumbs or the fixed contact bar of one post or page. Only the post being viewed is affected, never lists or query loops.
  • The CSS screen no longer causes a PHP deprecation notice when opened while custom CSS is switched off.
  • The recommended settings on the Get started tab include format sets and per-page display settings.

0.13.0

  • New blocks: accordion, FAQ, description list, tabs, steps and caption box (off until switched on under Blocks). Accordions open without JavaScript, tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, steps are saved as an ordered list, and the FAQ block can add FAQPage structured data.
  • New block settings under Design: show on phones or computers only, space below blocks and text highlights (marker, font size, small note, no line break, clear formatting).
  • Table: merge and split cells, switch cells between th and td, make the first column of the body row headers and repair broken rows, all saved in core’s own cell attributes. Keep the header row in view with CSS position: sticky, together with sideways scrolling. A minimum width for every column, centering across or down only, centered header text and a color for header cells in the body.
  • The recommended settings on the Get started tab include the new blocks and settings.

0.12.0

  • New “Get started” tab, first in the KUMITATE screen: create the finished sample of a trade child theme, switch on the recommended features in one click, and enter the site identity.
  • The dashboard and the theme screen point to the finished sample of the active child theme until it is created or dismissed.
  • After the sample is created, buttons lead to the draft pages, the home page setting and the Site Editor.
  • The Site identity screen can switch structured data on where it says it is off.
  • The CSS screen is listed in the menu only while custom CSS is switched on.
  • Search titles and descriptions: category, tag, taxonomy, post type and blog listings get a canonical link built from the listing itself (WordPress prints one on single posts and pages only).
  • Structured data: no second breadcrumb list on WooCommerce pages, which describe their own.

0.11.0

  • New: fixed contact bar block for booking, telephone and LINE buttons (off until switched on under Navigation).

0.10.5

  • Prepared for the WordPress.org plugin directory: updates now come from WordPress.org.

0.10.4

  • Hardened request handling and output escaping on the settings and starter screens (no change in behavior).

0.10.3

  • Settings screens reworked: features as cards with switches and an on/off badge, the number of features switched on shown on each tab, and one save button kept at the bottom of the screen that says when there are unsaved changes and asks before leaving.
  • The SEO tab starts with where things stand (who outputs the tags, what is not entered yet with a link to where it is entered, the basic setup) and saves the switches and the search and sharing settings together. Settings open as their switches are turned on, grouped in sections with links at the top; the table of where each setting lives folds away.
  • The Site identity screen uses the same cards, logo preview and save bar.
  • “Settings saved.” now appears on every tab.

0.10.2

  • Description length: descriptions longer than the set length (120 by default) are shortened when output, written ones included, ending on a sentence where possible. The saved text is kept whole; 0 outputs descriptions as written.
  • WebPage carries the page image as image as well as primaryImageOfPage.
  • The settings route accepts POST, PUT and PATCH from administrators: features, search settings and site identity, only the parts sent, with the same checks as the screens. An unknown key refuses the whole request; a value that does not pass keeps the saved one and is listed as dropped.

0.10.1

  • WooCommerce shop: the shop page’s own title, description, image and search listing now apply to the shop, which WooCommerce shows as the product archive. Before, a noindex set there left the sitemap but never reached the page.
  • Sharing image by address, for an image outside the media library such as a theme preview; its size is read when the file is on this site.
  • Without a page image, featured image or site default, sharing falls back to the site logo (Site identity, theme logo) or site icon, at least 200 pixels, in the small card. The large card is used only for a wide image of at least 600 pixels.
  • Structured data: BlogPosting.image and WebPage.primaryImageOfPage use the same image as sharing. The publisher logo falls back to the theme logo or site icon when none is chosen on the Site identity screen.
  • Author archives can be switched off: /author/name/ and /?author=N go to the front page with a 301, links to them too, and the author sitemap is left out.
  • A category or tag none of whose posts is listed in search gets noindex and leaves the sitemap; it follows its posts as they change.
  • A character count with the guide under title and description fields on the classic editor, term and settings screens, and a note when a description is longer than the guide.
  • A “Not entered yet” list on the SEO tab: default sharing image, publisher logo, profiles.
  • GET /wp-json/kumitate-site-tools/v1/settings reports the switches, who outputs the tags, the search settings and the site identity to administrators. Read-only.

0.10.0

  • Search titles and descriptions: a title per page, per term and for the front page, title formats per content type and for archives (%title%, %site%, %page%) through WordPress’s own title filters, and a meta description from the page’s own setting, the hand-written excerpt or the start of the text. Automatic text comes only from paragraphs, lists and quotes, never runs shortcodes or dynamic blocks, ends on a sentence within about 120 characters and is cached with a fingerprint of the content. Written descriptions are never cut.
  • Social sharing: Open Graph and X card tags with the page’s own sharing image, its featured image or a site default, including width, height and alt text; the small card when there is no image. Nothing is shared from protected, private or preview pages.
  • Search listing: noindex per page, per term, per content type and for author and date archives, only ever added, never lifting a noindex from WordPress or another plugin. The WordPress sitemap leaves out the same pages and terms at query time, so lists and page counts agree, along with password-protected posts and WooCommerce cart, checkout and account pages.
  • A “Search and sharing” panel in the post sidebar, a box in the classic editor and fields on term screens; the values are registered meta available in the REST API in edit context to users who may edit the item.
  • All three are off by default. A “Use the basic setup” button switches them on together after listing what changes. An active SEO plugin takes precedence; after it is deactivated KUMITATE waits to be chosen again instead of taking over.
  • The WebPage and BlogPosting structured data carry the same description as the meta tag when KUMITATE writes it.

0.9.0

  • Site identity screen: the publisher as Organization or Person with name, description, logo or photo and profiles elsewhere (sameAs), and how post authors are stated. Structured data becomes one connected graph: publisher, WebSite, WebPage per page, BreadcrumbList and BlogPosting linked by @id.
  • Business info block: type of business, name, address, telephone, email, opening hours, price range, map link, reservation button and a photo. With structured data on, the block adds a local business node of the chosen schema.org type to the graph; a single shop published by an organisation becomes that organisation’s node, several shops become separate places under it. Only what the block shows is structured, and the structured data is now printed in the footer so a block anywhere on the page, including a footer template part, is included.
  • Block titles, descriptions and keywords now really appear in Japanese in the editor: WordPress looks those up with a gettext context, which the bundled translation lacked before. Translations are also loaded before the blocks register.
  • Table of contents and link card blocks, both built from the page when it is shown, so nothing stale is ever saved. Headings get their anchors at render time only inside the content of the page the table of contents is on.
  • SEO division of labour: the settings tab reports the active SEO plugin, recommends SEO SIMPLE PACK when none is installed, and lists where each setting lives. Structured data stays on next to SEO SIMPLE PACK and reuses its per-post description; it still turns off next to plugins that output their own JSON-LD.
  • Table reading aids grew into a full set: scroll sideways always or only on narrow screens, with a hint on phones; keep the first column in view while scrolling; stack cells on phones; center every cell; set the table width and the first column width; color the header row and the first column from the theme palette or any color; and a “Simple lines” block style.
  • Values are stored in one block attribute and become CSS variables at render time. The saved table markup is untouched, so a table never becomes invalid and the plugin being off leaves a standard table.
  • Colors chosen from the palette are stored by slug, so they follow a child theme switch.
  • Cell marks for comparison tables: a symbol (◎ ○ △ × ✓ − ?), an optional cell background from the palette or any color, and white text for dark backgrounds, all from the cell’s text toolbar. The symbol is a real character, so it is read aloud and copied like any text.
  • Two more patterns built from the above: a plan comparison table that scrolls sideways on phones, and a pros-and-cons table that stacks on phones.
  • A custom CSS screen with common, front-end and editor parts. Suggestions as you type merge Emmet expansions (m10 becomes margin: 10px;) with CSS properties and values; Tab expands, Ctrl+Space opens the list. CodeMirror highlighting and CSSLint, a dark look by default with a light option and text size, both remembered per browser. Off by default; stored by the plugin so it survives a child theme switch; markup is refused on save.

0.8.0

  • Added a Breadcrumbs block and a Post Sharing block, so both can be placed in the Site Editor instead of relying on where the theme puts them.
  • A placed block suppresses the KUMITATE theme’s automatic insertion, so a page never shows the same breadcrumbs twice.
  • The shortcodes and the theme’s automatic insertion keep working with the same markup, so an existing site can move over at its own pace, or not at all.
  • Both blocks accept the standard spacing, font size and colour controls. Turning the feature off stops new insertions and hides the output, and a block already placed stays in the template.
  • Translated the block titles, descriptions and keywords, which were not reaching the translation files before. This also fixes the image slide block’s title.

0.7.0

  • Renamed the plugin folder, main file and text domain to kumitate-site-tools, and the display name to KUMITATE Site Tools.
  • Switched the source strings to English and bundled Japanese translations, so the admin, the block settings and the patterns read in the site’s language.
  • Made two strings translatable that were previously fixed text: the pre-publish checklist, and the separator between a field name and its error.
  • The image slide block’s default description is now “Image slide”. Saved blocks keep the description they already have, and it stays editable in the block sidebar.
  • Unchanged for existing sites: the option key, block name, CSS classes, shortcodes and filter names. Saved content and settings are kept.

0.6.0

  • Added table reading aids for the core table block: horizontal scrolling, minimum width and first-column emphasis, stored in the standard className.
  • Added pricing, services and contact patterns built from core blocks only.
  • Both features default to off, so existing sites are untouched.

Earlier

  • Development releases before 0.6.0 were not published and have no separate changelog.

short_description: Optional blocks and site tools for block themes. Turn each feature on or off; saved content stays as core blocks.
description:
KUMITATE Site Tools adds site building features to any block theme, one switch at a time. Nothing is enabled for you: open Settings and turn on only what a site needs.

The plugin extends core blocks instead of replacing them. Table settings are stored in the standard className, and the bundled patterns are built from core blocks only, so a page keeps working as ordinary block content after the feature is switched off or the plugin is deactivated.

Features, grouped by tab:

  • Table reading aids. Horizontal scrolling, a header row kept in view, a minimum width for every column, first-column emphasis and cell merging for the core table block, set from the block sidebar with no class names to type. Merged cells and header cells are saved as standard table markup (colspan, rowspan, th), so they stay when the plugin is off.
  • Pricing, services and contact patterns. Generic layouts for any trade, built from core blocks. Replace the text, photos and links on the page.
  • Image slide block. Add, replace and reorder core image blocks inside a slide. Autoplay is off by default, pauses on hover, focus and hidden tabs, and does not run when the visitor asks for reduced motion.
  • Breadcrumbs block. A real page and category hierarchy, never an invented primary category. Place it in the Site Editor, or let the KUMITATE theme position it for you.
  • Post sharing block for LINE, X and Facebook, shown on single posts, with an optional Copy URL button that confirms the copy on screen and to screen readers and falls back to a selected text box where copying is not available.
  • Table of contents block. Lists the page’s headings (H2, H2-H3 or H2-H4) with anchors added when the page is shown, numbered or plain, hidden below a chosen number of headings.
  • Link card block. Pick a post, page, category or tag by title; the card shows its image, title and summary, which can be replaced with your own, as a card, a slim line or plain text. It outputs nothing for a draft, private, removed or password-protected post.
  • Related pages list block. Posts from the same category or tag, or the child or sibling pages of a page, as cards, a list with small images or plain links, with the number, order, columns for phones and computers, a heading, the summary and the date. Built when the page is shown, in the content or in a Site Editor template; only published posts without a password are listed.
  • Automatic table of contents: added before the first heading of posts or other chosen types, when the page is shown. Left out where a table of contents block is placed or the page turns it off.
  • Automatic link cards: an address of a post or page of this site, pasted on its own line or embedded, is shown as a link card. Addresses of other sites are left alone and never fetched.
  • Structured data as one connected graph: publisher, WebSite, WebPage, BreadcrumbList and BlogPosting joined by @id. It works alongside SEO SIMPLE PACK and turns itself off when another plugin outputs structured data, so pages never carry two copies.
  • Analytics and site verification: fields for a Google Analytics 4 measurement ID, a Google Tag Manager container ID and the Search Console and Bing verification codes. Only the IDs are entered and checked; the plugin writes the tags. Nothing is output on admin screens, the login screen, feeds or the REST API.
  • Remove unneeded output: stop the emoji script, the WordPress version, the RSD, shortlink, REST API, embed discovery and feed links, and pingbacks to your own posts, one item at a time. Nothing is ticked by default.
  • Excerpt for pages: the excerpt box on pages, used in link cards, lists and the meta description.
  • Post list columns: featured image and search visibility columns in the post and page lists, with quick and bulk editing of search visibility. The search column is left out while another SEO plugin is in charge.
  • Search and sharing for sites without an SEO plugin: search titles and meta descriptions, Open Graph and X card tags, and noindex with the WordPress sitemap following it. Off by default, and they step aside for the major SEO plugins.
  • Accordion block. Items built on the browser’s own details and summary elements, so they open with a click, Enter or Space and can be read without JavaScript; the script only adds an animation and stays still when the visitor asks for reduced motion. Four styles, three CSS-drawn icon sets, titles as plain text or h2 to h6, and items that start open.
  • FAQ block. Questions and answers marked Q and A, in four styles, with square, rounded or round marks in the text color, the main color or a custom color, outlined or filled. Optional FAQPage structured data: one script per page built from the blocks.
  • Description list block. Terms and descriptions saved as dl, dt and dd, stacked, with a line on the left, side by side (term width 1 to 12em, stacked on phones) or as banded terms.
  • Tab block. Three styles, tab widths and sideways scrolling set separately for computers and phones, a first-open tab, background color and four border sets. Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with arrow, Home and End keys; without JavaScript every panel is shown in turn with its title.
  • Step block. Numbered steps saved as an ordered list, in three styles, with the first number, number shape or layout, a translatable label and the title element set on the list, and per-step overrides. A timeline style joins dates or times with a line, for a history, the flow of a day or an event programme, with an icon, fill, emphasis or color for each point.
  • Caption box block. A framed box with a caption, in seven styles and three color sets a theme can redefine with CSS custom properties. Kinds (information, hint, caution, alert, good example, bad example, memo) set the icon, color and caption at once, with colors made from the theme; an icon can also be added without a kind.
  • Speech balloon block. A face image, a name and the words in a balloon, speaking or thinking, filled or outlined. Saved speakers copy their image, name and look into a balloon, so editing a speaker never changes published posts.
  • Review block. A rating in half stars, points for and against, a summary, a price and a link, with optional Review structured data for products, services, shops, apps, books and courses.
  • Banner link block. A card with a title and a short text over a background image, all one link, with the text position, an overlay, a shape for computers and phones and a hover effect that respects reduced motion.
  • Box menu block. Linked boxes in a grid, each with an icon or an image and a label, with separate column counts for phones and computers.
  • Link list block. Links with an icon, lines between them and an optional arrow at the end.
  • Icon block. One large icon from the shared set, with a size, a color from the theme palette, a background shape (none, circle or rounded square; light, filled or outline), alignment, an optional link and a name for screen readers. Only the icon name is saved.
  • Icons: 34 line icons drawn for this plugin, no brand logos. Posts save only the icon’s name, so icons can be added or replaced with the siteframe_site_tools_icons filter.
  • Responsive columns block. One to six columns each for phones, tablets and computers, or a sideways scroll on phones that works with the keyboard. Converts to and from the core columns block.
  • Full-width section block. A background that reaches the screen edges on full-width templates, with an optional image, a tint and slanted, waved, peaked, arched or zigzag top and bottom edges. A separate background image and focal point can be set for phones; visitors download only one of the two.
  • Display conditions block. Shows the blocks inside only to logged-in or logged-out visitors, to chosen roles, within a period, on chosen kinds of page or for chosen categories and tags. Not a way to protect paid content. Placed blocks keep their conditions when the feature is off.
  • Show on phones or computers only: a block setting saved as an additional CSS class. The hiding styles keep loading on pages that use it even when the feature is switched off, so content never appears twice. The breakpoint follows the theme (782px) and can be filtered.
  • Space below blocks: a toolbar menu that sets a block’s bottom margin from the theme’s spacing sizes, stored as the core margin setting, and a panel with the space above and below for computers, tablets and phones. The computer size is core’s own margin, so it stays without the plugin.
  • Text highlights: marker, font size, small note, no line break, folder and file names, list lines and centred lines in table cells, a line break on phones only, letter spacing (narrow, wide or very wide) and a button that clears formatting. The formats stay registered when the feature is off, so saved text keeps its markup.
  • Format sets and editor settings: a KUMITATE > Editor settings screen for the marker shape and colors, three named format sets that apply several formats in one click, and up to ten custom formats whose classes you style in Additional CSS.
  • Block style collection: boxes, icon boxes, frames, border sets, list marks, section headings, image and video frames, a double-line table and framed columns for core blocks, colored by the theme. Only a class is saved, so styled blocks keep their content when the feature is off, and the CSS loads only on pages that use a style.
  • Your own block styles: name a style, choose the blocks it is offered on and pick its colors, border, corner radius, spacing, shadow and text size from a form, with a live preview. It appears under Styles in those blocks and is saved as the standard is-style-{name} class. Up to 20 styles.
  • Button styles and inline buttons: Raised, Rounded, Shadow, With arrow and Shine styles, an icon, a hover effect (lift, lighter, darker, moving arrow) that respects reduced motion and a width for phones, tablets and computers for the core button block, and linked text shown as a small button inside a line.
  • Column options for phones: two columns on phones and the space between stacked columns for the core columns block, saved as classes.
  • Editor helpers: a title length counter, a button that selects the parent list, and a per-user choice of which KUMITATE text toolbar buttons appear.
  • Per-page display settings (off by default): a “Display” panel in the post and page editor hides the title, featured image, date, categories, tags and author, sharing links, breadcrumbs or the fixed contact bar on that page only. Lists of posts and query loops are not affected. A hidden title stays available to screen readers and search engines unless the text has its own level 1 heading.
  • Default featured image: an image shown for posts without a featured image in query loop lists, link cards and related pages lists. Nothing is saved to the posts, and it is never used for sharing images or structured data.
  • Fixed contact bar block. Booking, telephone and LINE buttons kept at the bottom of the screen, on phones only or on every screen size, without JavaScript. Place it in the footer to show it on every page.
  • Business info block. Name, address, telephone, opening hours, a map link and a reservation button, described to search engines as a local business of the chosen type with the same details.
  • Settings export and import on the Get started tab: one JSON file with the plugin’s settings. Import checks every value like the settings screens and ignores unknown keys.

Colors, fonts and spacing come from the active theme’s presets. The plugin does not restyle body text or headings, and its CSS is scoped to its own blocks.

No license key, no domain activation, no purchase check, no expiry. Deactivating the plugin never deletes content or settings. No external fonts and no tracking by the plugin itself. Nothing is loaded from other servers unless you enter a Google Analytics or Google Tag Manager ID (see External services).

The plugin is optional for the KUMITATE theme and works with other block themes. Breadcrumbs and sharing are placed automatically in the KUMITATE theme’s templates; other themes can use the siteframe_breadcrumbs and siteframe_share shortcodes.

External services

This plugin connects to outside services only when you switch on Analytics and site verification and enter an ID. Nothing is sent while the feature is off or the fields are empty.

  • Google Analytics 4: with a measurement ID, every public page loads the Google tag (gtag.js) from www.googletagmanager.com, which sends visit data such as the page address, referrer, browser and device information to Google Analytics. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Google Tag Manager: with a container ID, every public page loads the container from www.googletagmanager.com, which runs the tags you set up in Tag Manager and sends the data those tags collect. Terms, Privacy Policy.

The Search Console and Bing verification codes are only written into a meta tag in the page head; the plugin sends nothing to Google or Microsoft for them.
